# Developer guide

Reference for the templates in detail: what each one does, its inputs and outputs, how it is
built, and the pitfalls we've already run into. For the contribution workflow and local
validation commands see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). The source of truth for inputs
is each workflow's `on.workflow_call.inputs`. Keep the tables below in sync with it.

- [ansible-role-ci.yml](#ansible-role-ciyml)
- [ansible-role-release.yml](#ansible-role-releaseyml)
- [ansible-role-galaxy.yml](#ansible-role-galaxyyml)
- [docker-ci.yml](#docker-ciyml)
- [docker-release.yml](#docker-releaseyml)
- [Repo design](#repo-design)
- [Known gotchas](#known-gotchas)

## ansible-role-ci.yml

`ansible-lint` and `molecule test` across a matrix of `ansible-core` versions, plus an
end-to-end install job (no container) on Linux and macOS. `molecule` and `end2end` detect
whether the caller has `molecule/default/molecule.yml` / `tests/e2e/playbook.yml` and no-op
when they're absent, so the workflow is safe to adopt before those scenarios exist.

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ansible_versions` | `["2.14",…,"2.21"]` | JSON array of `ansible-core` minors to test |
| `lint_os` | `["ubuntu-latest","macos-latest"]` | JSON array of runner OSes for `ansible-lint` |
| `e2e_os` | `["ubuntu-latest","macos-latest"]` | JSON array of runner OSes for the end-to-end job |
| `e2e_python_version` | `"3.14"` | Python used to install `ansible-core` for the end-to-end job |

Callers that want the molecule JUnit report posted as a check need `permissions: checks: write`
on the caller job.

## ansible-role-release.yml

Manual release: bumps `config.json`, regenerates the README and `meta/argument_specs.yml`
via `ansible-docsmith`, updates `CHANGELOG.md` via `git-cliff`, tags, and creates a GitHub
Release.

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_type:
        type: choice
        default: patch
        options: [patch, minor, major, custom]
      custom_version:
        type: string

jobs:
  release:
    uses: m13tLabs/gh-actions-templates/.github/workflows/ansible-role-release.yml@main
    with:
      release_type: ${{ inputs.release_type }}
      custom_version: ${{ inputs.custom_version }}
      app_id: ${{ vars.CI_APP_ID }}
    secrets: inherit
```

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | (required) | GitHub App ID, e.g. `${{ vars.CI_APP_ID }}` |
| `release_type` | `"patch"` | `patch`, `minor`, `major` or `custom` |
| `custom_version` | `""` | Explicit version, required when `release_type: custom` |
| `default_branch` | `"develop"` | Branch released from and pushed back to |
| `readme_filename` | `"README.md"` | README regenerated by `ansible-docsmith` (case-sensitive) |
| `draft_release` | `true` | Create the GitHub Release as a draft |

Secret: `CI_PRIVATE_KEY`.

## ansible-role-galaxy.yml

Triggers an Ansible Galaxy import of the calling repo on tag push. The repository is derived
from `github.repository`, so the same caller file works in every role repo.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags: ["*"]

jobs:
  release:
    uses: m13tLabs/gh-actions-templates/.github/workflows/ansible-role-galaxy.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
```

Secret: `ANSIBLE_GALAXY_API_TOKEN`.

## docker-ci.yml

`actionlint`, then `hadolint` plus a single-arch `docker buildx` build (loaded and
smoke-tested) per Dockerfile, matrixed over `dockerfiles`. The smoke test is a caller-supplied
shell one-liner with `$IMAGE` set to that build's local tag. Each Dockerfile is also built
(not loaded) for `platforms` to catch multi-arch failures before release.

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `image_name` | `"ci-image"` | Local tag prefix the CI builds are loaded as |
| `context` | `"."` | Docker build context |
| `dockerfiles` | `'["Dockerfile"]'` | JSON array of Dockerfile paths (relative to `context`) |
| `build_args` | `""` | Newline-separated build args applied to every build |
| `smoke_test` | `docker run --rm "$IMAGE" --help` | Shell run once per Dockerfile with `$IMAGE` set; `""` skips it |
| `platforms` | `"linux/amd64,linux/arm64"` | Platforms for the extra multi-arch build; `""` skips it |
| `dockerfile_platforms` | `'{}'` | JSON object overriding `platforms` per Dockerfile, e.g. `'{"Dockerfile.gpu":"linux/amd64"}'` |
| `dockerhub` | `false` | Log in to Docker Hub before building (needs `DOCKER_HUB_USER` / `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN`) |
| `runs_on` | `"ubuntu-latest"` | Runner for every job |

How it's built:

- The multi-arch build runs without `setup-qemu-action`, so arm64 runs under buildkit's
  built-in QEMU exactly as in `docker-release.yml`. That emulator doesn't preserve argv[0],
  which breaks uutils (Ubuntu 26.04+) `env` in `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebangs on arm64 only
  (`ai-agent-for-gitlab`'s agent image hit this mid-release). Keep the QEMU setup of both
  Docker templates in sync, or CI stops reproducing the release.
- The GHA cache scope is keyed on `context/dockerfile` when `context != '.'`, so a repo
  calling the workflow once per image directory doesn't thrash a shared `Dockerfile` scope.

## docker-release.yml

Manual release: bumps the version file, updates `CHANGELOG.md` via `git-cliff`, builds a
multi-arch image, pushes every ref in `images` tagged `X.Y.Z` / `X.Y` / `latest`, attests
build provenance per image, and creates a GitHub Release. Passes `APP_VERSION` and
`BUILD_DATE` as build args.

`variant_dockerfile` builds and pushes a second image (e.g. a GPU build) with the same tags
plus `variant_suffix` (`X.Y.Z-gpu`, `latest-gpu`, …) and its own attestation. To ship two
differently named images from separate directories under one version, changelog and
Release, point `variant_context` / `variant_images` at the second one and set
`variant_suffix: ''` (`ai-agent-for-gitlab` does this for `gitlab-app/` + `agent-image/`).

| Input | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `images` | (required) | JSON array of image refs to tag, push and attest |
| `client_id` | (required) | GitHub App client ID, e.g. `${{ vars.CI_CLIENT_ID }}` |
| `release_type` | `"patch"` | `patch`, `minor`, `major` or `custom` |
| `custom_version` | `""` | Explicit version, required when `release_type: custom` |
| `default_branch` | `"develop"` | Branch released from and pushed back to |
| `version_file` | `"config.json"` | JSON file with a top-level `version` key |
| `bump_command` | `""` | Shell run after the bump with `$RELEASE_VERSION` set; tracked files it changes join the release commit |
| `context` | `"."` | Docker build context |
| `dockerfile` | `"Dockerfile"` | Main Dockerfile, relative to `context` |
| `platforms` | `"linux/amd64,linux/arm64"` | Comma-separated build platforms |
| `variant_dockerfile` | `""` | Optional second Dockerfile; `""` disables the variant |
| `variant_suffix` | `"-gpu"` | Tag suffix for the variant images |
| `variant_context` | `""` | Variant build context; `""` means `context` |
| `variant_images` | `""` | JSON array of variant image refs; `""` means `images` |
| `variant_platforms` | `""` | Variant build platforms; `""` means `platforms` |
| `dockerhub` | `false` | Log in to Docker Hub before pushing |
| `draft_release` | `true` | Create the GitHub Release as a draft |

| Output | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `release_version` | The released version (`X.Y.Z`) |
| `release_sha` | SHA of the pushed release commit. Check this out in follow-up jobs (e.g. a Helm chart publish), since a draft release has no `v<version>` tag yet |

Secrets: `CI_PRIVATE_KEY`, plus `DOCKER_HUB_USER` / `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` when `dockerhub: true`.
GHCR uses the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

How it's built:

- The provenance attestation fans out over `images` via a matrix. The variant gets its own
  `attest-variant` job keyed off the `variant_digest` job output, which is an empty string
  when the variant steps (gated on `inputs.variant_dockerfile != ''`) are skipped.
- `bump_command` runs via `env` + `bash -euo pipefail -c`, never with `${{ inputs.* }}`
  spliced into the script. It's followed by `git add -u`, so only *tracked* files join the
  release commit. A new file it creates is silently left out.

## Repo design

`pipeline.yml` runs actionlint and calls `ansible-role-ci.yml` against a minimal, throwaway
Ansible role at the repo root (`tasks/`, `meta/`, `molecule/default/`, `tests/e2e/`,
`.ansible-lint`). It is not a publishable role.

The fixture lives at the root because a reusable workflow's `actions/checkout` always checks
out the *caller's* repo at its root. There is no way to point `ansible-role-ci.yml` at a
subdirectory. A dedicated fixture repo pinned via `@<branch-or-sha>` was considered and
rejected for now (more infra, needs cross-repo dispatch/token).

The other templates aren't self-tested. The release/Galaxy ones push commits and tags and
create real releases, and `docker-ci.yml` needs a real `Dockerfile` at the caller's root.
Validate them against a consumer repo, see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#templates-without-a-self-test).

## Known gotchas

Schema and tooling:

- `workflow_call` inputs only support `type: boolean | number | string`. `type: choice` and
  `options:` are `workflow_dispatch`-only. Using them on a `workflow_call` input makes the
  workflow invalid, and it won't run at all when called.
- An input can't be both `required: true` and carry a `default:`. The default is unreachable
  and actionlint flags it.
- `actions/create-github-app-token@v3` authenticates with **either** `app-id` **or**
  `client-id`, plus `private-key`. actionlint (through at least v1.7.12) ships a stale input
  snapshot that only knows `app-id`, so `pipeline.yml` and local runs pass `-ignore` regexes
  for both resulting messages. Drop them once actionlint refreshes its metadata.

Shell:

- `run:` blocks execute under `bash -e`. A conditional like
  `[ -f file ] && pip install -r file` as the **last** line fails the step whenever the file
  is missing, because the compound statement's status is non-zero. The molecule job's
  "Install dependencies" step broke this way for repos without
  `molecule/default/requirements.txt`. It now ends with a trailing `true`. The same pattern in
  the lint job is safe only because an unconditional `pip install ansible-lint` follows it.
  Keep something unconditional last.

Tokens:

- GitHub App tokens are capped at 1 hour. Multi-arch QEMU builds in `docker-release.yml` can
  outlast the token minted at job start, so the final push failed with
  `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'`. The workflow mints a fresh token
  (`app-token-push`) right before `Push commits` and uses it for the push and
  `Create Release on GH`.
- The molecule "Publish test report" step (`mikepenz/action-junit-report@v6`) logs
  `Resource not accessible by integration` when the caller lacks `checks: write` (true for
  `pipeline.yml`'s `self-test`). That's non-fatal: `require_tests`, `fail_on_failure` and
  `fail_on_parse_error` all default to `false`, so the fixture needs no JUnit output.

Releases:

- Generate `RELEASE_NOTES.md` with `git-cliff --tag v<new> --unreleased`, **not**
  `--latest`. `--latest` renders the newest *existing* tag's section and ignores `--tag`, so
  `ai-agent-for-gitlab`'s 0.2.2 Release shipped 0.2.0's notes.
- `draft_release: true` creates no git tag until the draft is published. If a draft is
  deleted instead (0.2.1 in `ai-agent-for-gitlab`), no tag is left behind, and the next
  release's changelog includes those commits again.
